people.role: Co-founder and Co-chairman, Oaktree Capital Management

people.name: Daniel Baer
people.role: Former U.S. Ambassador to the OSCE and Interim President, Carnegie Endowment for International Peace

briefings.tldr: The bond market is flashing red with 10-year Treasury yields hitting a 19-year high above 5.1%, driven by stubborn inflation, massive national debt, and heavy capital demand from AI investments.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
The bond market is flashing red with 10-year Treasury yields hitting a 19-year high above 5.1%, driven by stubborn inflation, massive national debt, and heavy capital demand from AI investments. Meanwhile, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have driven Brent crude above $103 per barrel, and AI data center provider SB Energy has delayed its $50 billion IPO due to weak investor demand.

## Market Vitals and Bond Market Pressures
* **Market Indices & Yield Spikes:** Major indices declined as US treasuries sold off, with the 10-year Treasury yield rising above 5.1% (a 19-year high), the 30-year yield returning to 2004 levels, and the 5-year yield breaching 5%.
* **Federal Reserve Rate Hike Odds:** On Cali, the odds of another rate hike next month rose to 66%, and the odds of a third hike later in the year rose to 34%.
* **Treasury Intervention:** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessant executed a $6 billion long-dated bond buyback program with another $6 billion operation scheduled, which Howard Marks criticized as a cosmetic fix unable to solve structurally unsound economic problems.
* **Historical Interest Rates (Howard Marks):** Today's 5.3% to 5.4% 30-year bond yields are historically low rather than high, with the recent era of zero interest rates (2009–2021) representing an aberration.

## Drivers of Rising Bond Yields & Deficits
* **Stubborn Inflation:** Inflation has consistently remained above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for the last five years, creating a need for purchasing power protection.
* **National Debt & Deficits (Howard Marks):** The US national debt has reached $40 trillion, running an annual deficit approaching $2 trillion during a period of economic prosperity and low unemployment.
* **Competing Capital Demand:** AI is drawing hundreds of billions of dollars from the debt market, actively competing with the US Treasury for capital.
* **International Comparison:** Japan has run massive debts for a long time without acute financial market failures, but US fiscal profligacy ("golden credit card" behavior) risks long-term currency debasement and a demand for higher risk compensation from foreign investors.

## Geopolitical Tensions & Energy Markets
* **UN General Assembly Standoffs:** President Trump stated he could annihilate the Islamic Republic quickly, while Iran's President Masud Peskian asserted they would never bow their head or bend at the knee.
* **Middle East Energy Impact:** The Strait of Hormuz remains closed and US blockades continue against Iranian ports, pushing Brent crude above $103 per barrel (up over 40% since the war began).
* **Global Food and Energy Vulnerability (Daniel Baer):** The combination of the Iran war (driving up diesel and transport costs) and paralyzed Black Sea wheat exports from Russia and Ukraine creates a "double whammy" threatening millions with high food prices or food shortages.
* **Midterm Elections Impact (Daniel Baer):** Political pressures surrounding the US midterms influence bargaining incentives, with adversaries and partners closely watching the vulnerability of an American president.

## SB Energy IPO Delay
* **Valuation & Banker Struggles:** AI data center provider SB Energy delayed its IPO this month after bankers struggled to find buyers at the target $50 billion valuation (making it purportedly more valuable than PayPal, Honda, or Chipotle).
* **Operational Reality:** The company currently has zero data centers in operation; less than 10% of its planned data centers are under construction, while over 90% have not broken ground.
* **Revenue Backlog Discrepancies:** While claiming a revenue backlog of over $400 billion, only $1 billion is expected within the next 2 years, over 80% is projected past 8 years from now, and some portions extend past 20 years.
* **Shrinking Core Business:** SB Energy's existing revenue primarily stems from its solar business, which saw revenues fall more than 8% last year.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Interest Rate Trajectory:** Interest rates will probably not go down much, if at all, in the coming year or two (*Howard Marks*).
* **Energy Cost Projections:** Even if the Strait of Hormuz were fully reopened, added insurance costs and tolling mechanisms mean energy prices and crude oil are unlikely to return to pre-war levels in the medium term (*Daniel Baer*).

## Notable Quotes
> "Today's interest rates are not high. A 5.3 or 4% 30-year bond is very low relative to history. It's only high relative to recent history. And I argue strenuously that the recent history of interest rates is the aberration." 
> — *Howard Marks*

> "Things take longer to happen than we thought they would, but then they happen faster than we thought they could." 
> — *Howard Marks*

> "Even if there were a deal that quote unquote fully reopened the straight of Hormuz it would take some time both to work through the backlog and also for there to be enough trust that the straight is actually safe for shipping... we can make the prediction that the energy prices are unlikely... to come back down to those pre-war levels." 
> — *Daniel Baer*

briefings.title: China Could Have Crushed the U.S. Economy. Why Didn't It?
briefings.tldr: President Xi Jinping’s high-stakes state visit to Washington highlights a strategic stalemate between the U.S. and China, where neither side can deliver a knockout blow, prompting an ongoing debate among experts regarding whether a durable détente or escalating K-shaped competition defines the future of the relationship.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
President Xi Jinping’s high-stakes state visit to Washington highlights a strategic stalemate between the U.S. and China, where neither side can deliver a knockout blow, prompting an ongoing debate among experts regarding whether a durable détente or escalating K-shaped competition defines the future of the relationship.

## 1. The 2015-2025 Context & Xi Jinping’s Washington Visit
- **State Visit Dynamics:** Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington kicks off Thursday morning, September 24th, marking his first state visit to Washington since 2015.
- **Beijing's Anxieties:** **Julian Gewirtz** notes that planning has been much slower and more slipshod than under previous administrations, causing high anxiety in Beijing.
- **Presidential Deference:** **Julian Gewirtz** highlights that President Trump is going above and beyond with optics, becoming the first American president to greet another leader at the Joint Base Andrews tarmac—an honor typically reserved for popes or close allies.
- **The State Dinner Guest List:** **Julian Gewirtz** notes that the state dinner will feature a parade of senior American corporate executives and billionaire friends of the president, occurring just 40 days before midterms where Republicans could flip one or both houses of Congress.
- **Xi's Objectives:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** assesses that Xi is seeking an extension of the trade truce and prolonged stability ahead of the important party congress next year, while managing domestic preoccupations and navigating Trump's unpredictability.

## 2. The Trade Truce and Strategic Stalemate
- **Escalation Timeline:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** details the escalation cycle leading to the truce:
  - **April:** Liberation Day tariffs followed by Chinese retaliation with restrictions on rare earths and permanent magnets.
  - **October:** The U.S. expanded export controls on affiliates of entity-listed Chinese companies.
  - **China's Response:** Sweeping restrictions on rare earths and permanent magnets that threatened the global economy.
  - **Busan Truce:** The two sides reached a truce pausing escalatory controls, which has remained in effect until today.
- **The K-Shaped Relationship:** **Julian Gewirtz** describes the U.S.–China relationship as "K-shaped," meaning it is accelerating in two directions simultaneously: leader-level diplomacy and targeted stabilization on the upward leg, with intensifying competitive pressures below on the downward leg.
- **A Durable Détente vs. Coexistence:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** argues for embracing a durable détente that abandons disruptive fantasies of decisive victory, noting that neither side can land a knockout blow and both must cohabit the planet. Conversely, **Julian Gewirtz** doubts a durable détente is possible under Trump, arguing Beijing is attempting to raise and remake the floor to constrain future American policy.

## 3. Policy Prescriptions and Taiwan
- **Advice for President Trump:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** advises Trump to stay away from the issue of Taiwan altogether, noting it should not be treated as a bargaining chip, and to pursue regular and sustained technical dialogue on AI safety alongside working on wins for American farmers.
- **Polling and Public Opinion:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** cites a recent Chicago Council poll showing a majority of Americans (57%) favor cooperation and engagement with China, compared to 40% wanting to limit China's power.
- **The Competition Label:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** critiques "competition" as a poorly defined buzzword, preferring terms like deterrence and conflicting interests regarding Taiwan to avoid zero-sum escalation dominance. **Julian Gewirtz** counters that competition is an undeniable dynamic and diagnosis of reality that any coherent strategy must reckon with.
- **Bipartisan Consensus Shift:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** expresses surprise at how quickly Trump turned on a dime from escalatory tariffs to pursuing a good relationship with Xi, and how Republicans have gone along with it, suggesting the bipartisan hawkish consensus was not as hardened as it appeared. **Julian Gewirtz** emphasizes that future administrations of any political stripe will inherit a very different starting point regarding domestic strengths and alliances.

## 4. AI Safety and Strategic Intentions
- **Parallel AI Safety:** **Julian Gewirtz** argues that the U.S. and China should develop AI safety in parallel rather than jointly, as neither government has fully figured out how to govern the technologies domestically.
- **Conflicting Concepts of Control:** **Julian Gewirtz** and **Jessica Chen Weiss** note a fundamental divergence in risk perception: American labs focus on human control over models, whereas China's paramount concern is party control over models and societal stability. **Jessica Chen Weiss** adds that China's regulators classify "extreme loss of control" as a paramount risk to political control, yet the AI safety communities see potential for technical best-practice and threat-information sharing.
- **Intentions and Global Strategy:** **Julian Gewirtz** points to Xi Jinping's intensive diplomatic outreach—visiting the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SEO) in Central Asia, BRICS in India, and making a state visit to Egypt—as evidence that China is actively building alternative institutions where it is the central player, putting the U.S. in the position of a spectator.
- **Domestic Imperatives:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** argues in her forthcoming book, *What China Wants*, that Beijing is driven primarily by domestic imperatives (sovereignty, security, development) rather than a grand design to global hegemony. She notes that China chose not to crush the U.S. economy despite having the leverage to do so via permanent magnet and rare earth export controls, proving its priority is stability and development.

## 5. Quick Hits: Taiwan, Iran, and Russia
- **Taiwan Military Action:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** predicts that while kinetic bloodshed is unlikely, grey-zone military actions short of the kinetic threshold will undoubtedly continue.
- **Iran and Bargaining:** **Julian Gewirtz** warns against reports that Xi Jinping may link an offer to help the U.S. on Iran with unilateral concessions on Taiwan (such as the pending $14 billion arms package), calling it a "win-win" where Beijing wins twice by benefiting from a reopened Strait of Hormuz while securing concessions on Taiwan.
- **Russia Partnership:** **Jessica Chen Weiss** asserts that China views a surviving Putin as vital strategic ballast and insurance against a U.S. policy bent on coercion and containment. **Julian Gewirtz** notes that the personal and geopolitical partnership remains robust, with rumors pointing to a potential trilateral meeting among Putin, Xi, and Trump if Trump travels to Shenzhen for APEC later this year.

## Notable Quotes

> "You know, normally you trade symbolism for substance. You give a little honor. You want to get something in return. And and my core question is, well, what is the United States actually getting in return for all of those actions?"
> — Julian Gewirtz

> "The equilibrium will be more achievable if the Chinese side doesn't constantly feel like the United States is out to strangle China and perpetually keep China behind."
> — Jessica Chen Weiss

> "Future administrations... will be inheriting the keys to a quieter house in a quieter neighborhood, but discovering that a lot of the lease was written by Beijing."
> — Julian Gewirtz

> "China could have crushed the U.S. economy had it continued to restrict the export of of permanent magnets and rare earths, but it chose not to. And I think it reveals that what China wants is more influence, development and stability rather than to, you know, crush one of its biggest export markets, the United States."
> — Jessica Chen Weiss

briefings.title: Fireside Chat with Mark Moffat, CEO of IFS | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: IFS CEO Mark Moffat and Bank of America Managing Director Thomas Köhrer discussed how industrial AI is transforming asset-heavy, mission-critical sectors like manufacturing, aerospace, and utilities, emphasizing that true deployment requires a balance of probabilistic AI reasoning and deterministic safety standards where failure is not an option.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
IFS CEO Mark Moffat and Bank of America Managing Director Thomas Köhrer discussed how industrial AI is transforming asset-heavy, mission-critical sectors like manufacturing, aerospace, and utilities, emphasizing that true deployment requires a balance of probabilistic AI reasoning and deterministic safety standards where failure is not an option.

## Speakers & Roles
- **Mark Moffat** — CEO, IFS (Industrial software executive with a 28-year background spanning 24 years in tech services and 4 years at IFS)
- **Thomas Köhrer** — Managing Director, Bank of America (Panel moderator and discussion lead)

## IFS Company Profile & Strategy
- **Asset-Heavy Focus:** IFS has a 40-year history supporting capital-intensive, asset-heavy industries across the asset and service lifecycle, including utilities, manufacturing, aerospace, defense, service-based industries, mining, oil, and gas.
- **Scale & Retention:** The company operates with a 96% Gross Retention Rate (GRR) and supports 100% of commercial aviation flights in the US, carrying 800 million passengers annually.
- **Forward Deployed Engineering:** Pre-sales teams and developers spend extensive time on-site in warehouses and field ride-alongs to identify pinch points, leakage, and cost optimization opportunities in complex industrial value chains.

## Industrial AI vs. Enterprise AI
- **Penetration Gap:** While software engineering, legal, finance, and customer contact centers have heavily benefited from frontier models, industrial value chains remain relatively less penetrated.
- **Deterministic vs. Probabilistic:** Due to strict health, safety, and operational standards (e.g., jet engine maintenance requiring 99.99999% reliability), industrial AI must bridge probabilistic AI thinking with deterministic execution.
- **Sovereign & Agnostic Architecture:** Moffat noted that relying on a single frontier model is negligent; IFS uses an agnostic supply chain approach combining closed frontier models, open-source models, lower-parameter models deployed at the edge, and robotics.

## Case Study: Greenall (Grants Distillery)
- **Deployment & Impact:** Working with Grants (the second-largest global distiller, producing Hendricks gin and other brands) at a new distillery on the west coast of Scotland, IFS ingested design, engineering, PLM, schematics, telematics, and plant telemetry.
- **Results:** Regression-analyzed failure predictions across flow rates, temperature, throughput, volume, and gas reduced unplanned downtime by **38%**.
- **Speed of Execution:** The deal moved from first conversation to contract signature in just **8 days**.

## Boardroom Guidance & Future Outlook
- **Business Fundamentals:** Moffat advised boards to flip the perspective away from "AI for AI's sake" and instead focus on business fundamentals—solving profitability pinch points, performance deviations, and operational challenges.
- **Sovereignty & Geopolitics:** Sovereign AI is treated as an outcome achieved by maintaining supply-chain control over models and partnerships to navigate shifting national security and global political environments.
- **Industry Evolution:** Manufacturing—particularly global supply chain orchestration (production, materials, logistics, and fulfillment planning)—will undergo the most dramatic industry-wide transformation.

## Notable Quotes
> *"You can't vibe code how you think about maintenance of a jet engine... You have to be operating at 99.99999% degrees of reliability."* — Mark Moffat
> 
> *"I'm a software CEO, but I get confused as hell when I walk out there. I mean, there's a bunch of companies I've never heard of... Imagine you're not in the software industry. Imagine you're not in the AI industry. How the hell you navigate that? It's really difficult."* — Mark Moffat

briefings.title: LIVE: Mark Zuckerberg's Meta Connect 2026 keynote
briefings.tldr: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and executives unveiled Meta's expanding personal AI and wearables ecosystem at Meta Connect 2026, headlined by the personal AI agent Muse, new Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 styles, audio glasses, FDA-cleared hearing aids, and a breakthrough form factor of VR glasses.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and executives unveiled Meta's expanding personal AI and wearables ecosystem at Meta Connect 2026, headlined by the personal AI agent Muse, new Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 styles, audio glasses, FDA-cleared hearing aids, and a breakthrough form factor of VR glasses.

## Introduction and Vision for Personal Superintelligence
* **Optimistic AI Philosophy:** Mark Zuckerberg emphasized that Meta's core mission is to empower people, believing that the highest purpose of AI is creation and invention rather than automation, and that technology should be distributed widely.
* **Muse Personal Agent:** Launched a few weeks prior, Muse is designed as a personal agent providing its own secure virtual machine (**Muse Secure VM**) and specialized AI model (**Muse Spark**). 
* **Business Model:** Muse is offered free for a huge number of tokens, with Meta planning to profit over time by taking a small fee from transactions.

## Muse Ecosystem, Connectors, and Developer Platform
* **Alexander Wang on Growth:** Alexander Wang highlighted the explosive early growth of Muse, describing it as a "banger" with real-world savings and utility.
* **New Mac App & Computer Use:** The Muse Mac app launched with native dictation, and new computer use capabilities allow Muse to drive any app on a Mac.
* **Deep Retail & Service Integrations:** Meta announced major retail partnerships including Walmart, Best Buy, Dick's, Gap, Fanatics, Michael Kors, Sephora, Ulta, and Wayfair, alongside travel (Expedia), grocery (Instacart), and productivity tools (Box, GitHub, Granolah, Notion).
* **Payment Integrations:** Added support for Stripe, Shop Pay, and PayPal.
* **Open Connector Platform:** Opened up to developers, receiving over 1,500 applications in less than a week.

## Wearables, AI Glasses, and Hearing Enhancement
* **Shift to AI Glasses:** Zuckerberg explained that Meta has shifted its primary focus from the metaverse to building the best devices for personal superintelligence, positioning glasses as the ultimate AI form factor.
* **Real-Time Voice and Customization:** Meta introduced a state-of-the-art real-time voice model enabling custom voices, joyful animations, and background action execution.
* **Audio Glasses:** A new category of glasses without cameras, featuring open-ear audio, the longest battery life of any Meta glasses (full day), and a new Ray-Ban Clubmaster style.
* **Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3:** Slimmer frames, adjustable temple tips, Dolby Atmos spatial audio capture, six microphones, and an expanded lineup to 51 different style combinations starting at **$249**, adding Capri, Nova, and a Kylie ivory colorway, plus a Lisa collaboration collection.
* **Neural Band and Display Glasses:** Meta Ray-Ban display glasses with full-color high-resolution displays and the Meta neural band are catching up with demand and rolling out internationally.
* **FDA-Cleared Over-the-Counter Hearing Aid:** Hearing enhancement turns Meta glasses into an FDA-cleared hearing aid compensating for perceived mild to moderate hearing loss, featuring a guided in-app assessment.
* **Privacy and Security:** Introduced the **Muse Confidential VM** (where even Meta cannot see information) and private processing for glasses (starting with live translations) using the same technology as WhatsApp.

## Spatial Computing and Breakthrough VR Glasses
* **Andrew "Boz" Bosworth on VR Breakthrough:** Boz demonstrated Meta's new glasses-form-factor VR device featuring high-resolution displays, surface typing, hand/voice tracking, and assistant **Cooper**.
* **Entertainment and Cinema:** Certified as the first IMAX-enhanced VR device with Dolby Atmos and Dolby Vision. Disney Plus app coming later this year; Disney Immersive Cinema by ILM featuring Marvel Studios and Star Wars; plus apps from Peacock, Paramount Plus, HBO Max, YouTube, Prime Video, and Crunchyroll.
* **Live Sports & Gaming:** More than 100 immersive live events per year (including ESPN college football, MLB, UFC, TNT Sports, and NBC Sports). Features 75 hands-only gaming titles at launch, full Quest library support via optional attached controllers, and Xbox cloud gaming.
* **Hologram Calling:** Introduced full-body photorealistic holograms in VR (solving the legs problem) and bringing them to Meta Ray-Ban display glasses.
* **Pricing & Availability:** Priced at **$12.99** [sic: likely $1,299 based on context] and shipping in the spring.

## Muse Charm (Keychain AI)
* **Hardware Form Factor:** Zuckerberg revealed **Muse Charm**, a keychain-mounted hardware device packing the full Muse experience, real-time voice, and avatar stack with a fingerprint sensor.
* **Timeline:** Slated to ship in time for the holidays in **December**.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* "In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are used to accomplish their goals and improve their lives." — Mark Zuckerberg
* "In the coming years, most of these [nearly 2 billion people who wear glasses] are going to get upgraded to AI glasses." — Mark Zuckerberg
* "By the end of the year, we're going to have more than 100 different styles of glasses available." — Mark Zuckerberg

## Notable Quotes
> "Building is an act of love. It's how we impart what we believe, and we pour our hearts and our souls into what we make." 
> — Mark Zuckerberg

> "Muse has been saving real people, real money. Meta knows what it's like when a product is in the early days of crazy growth, and this one is, scientifically speaking, a banger." 
> — Alexander Wang

> "When there is background noise, I often cannot hear maybe every third or fourth word in a conversation. The hearing enhancement feature on these glasses can bring me into the present moment." 
> — Lindsay Jones

briefings.title: Lip-Bu Tan: Running an American Icon
briefings.channel: A Bit Personal with Jodi Shelton
briefings.tldr: Lip-Bu Tan shares his journey from a nuclear engineering student at MIT to a legendary venture capitalist and turnaround CEO of Cadence and Intel, emphasizing humility, deep personal discipline, and the power of collaborative partnerships over zero-sum competition.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Lip-Bu Tan shares his journey from a nuclear engineering student at MIT to a legendary venture capitalist and turnaround CEO of Cadence and Intel, emphasizing humility, deep personal discipline, and the power of collaborative partnerships over zero-sum competition.

## Early Life, Education, and Career Beginnings
- **Family Background:** Grew up in Malaysia as the youngest of five children to a strict, disciplined mother ("tiger mom") who instilled a strong work ethic. His siblings achieved extraordinary academic and professional success, including a Rhodes Scholar heart surgeon brother and a Harvard professor sister.
- **Academic Pivot:** Opted against following his brother into medicine, choosing to study nuclear engineering at MIT instead to tackle energy challenges.
- **Transition to Venture Capital:** After earning his MBA at the University of San Francisco while working as a CFO for a startup called Echo Energy (which he helped save), he founded Walden International with $3 million from family and friends, eventually scaling it to $5–6 billion under management.

## Leadership, Turnarounds, and Venture Philosophy
- **Venture Capital Approach:** Focuses on human character, integrity, coachability, and navigating near-death startup situations, looking for a 10x performance improvement and engagement with tier-one hyperscale customers (Amazon, Microsoft, Google).
- **Cadence Design Systems Turnaround:** Stepped in with no prior CEO experience, reading three "CEO for Dummies" books and responding personally to hundreds of daily employee emails to transform an ultra-introvert operating style and turn the company around.
- **Mentorship:** Credits Mushi (former CEO of Xilinx) with pivotal advice: making 70% of decisions correctly makes you a damn good CEO, which immediately lightened his mental burden.

## The Intel Turnaround and Government Relations
- **Returning to Intel:** Pulled out of retirement by a chief architect's text message: *"Before you retire, save Intel."* After receiving his wife's support, he took on the iconic company's massive operational challenges.
- **Meeting with President Trump:** After facing public pressure over past Chinese investments, he met with President Trump on a Monday at 4:00 PM, explained his background (US citizen for 40+ years), outlined a two-year turnaround strategy, and drew parallels to government backing for TSMC in Taiwan and companies in Singapore and Japan.

## Collaboration, Partnerships, and Industry Ecosystem
- **Partnership Philosophy:** Rejects viewing industry peers as competitors; works closely with leaders like Jensen Huang (Nvidia), Lisa Su (AMD), and CC Wei (TSMC).
- **TSMC Relationship:** Maintains close ties with Morris Chang (having worked alongside him for 40+ years) and notes that Intel remains a top-10 customer of TSMC while building its own foundry capabilities to serve booming AI demand.

## Personal Life, Faith, and Values
- **Daily Discipline & Fast Shifting:** Maintains a quiet, reserved demeanor rooted in his upbringing, combined with an ability to switch rapidly between complex topics at all hours of the night.
- **Family Support:** Celebrates 45 years of marriage with his wife, Issa, who keeps him grounded as his best friend and ultimate partner in supporting his career decisions.
- **Faith and Perspective:** Serves as a church elder in Berkeley; views daily pressures and quarterly earnings as simple checkpoints while remaining accountable to a higher purpose with peace of mind.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Intel Turnaround Timeline:** Lip-Bu Tan stated to President Trump that it would take **two years** to completely turn around Intel and execute the necessary operational changes (Attributed to Lip-Bu Tan).

## Notable Quotes
> "If you make 70% of the decision right, you're a damn good CEO."
> — Mushi (as recalled by Lip-Bu Tan)

> "With all your success at cadence... Intel is the iconic company it's so important for the industry and so important for United States. Before you retire, save Intel."
> — Chief Architect / Customer (as quoted by Lip-Bu Tan)

> "I never view people as competitor. Even what I like to win... it's not the zero game sum in the the business. You always try to find you can't do it all alone. You need partners and I always value partners."
> — Lip-Bu Tan

briefings.title: Meta Connect 2026: Developer State of the Union
briefings.tldr: Meta Connect 2026 announced major developer updates across four pillars—expanding the Muse AI model family and general availability of the Meta Model API, developer tools for Ray-Ban AI glasses with SDK and web app support, the V207 SDK for upcoming Meta VR Glasses, and the launch of Horizon Create and Studio for prompt-driven game development.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Meta Connect 2026 announced major developer updates across four pillars—expanding the Muse AI model family and general availability of the Meta Model API, developer tools for Ray-Ban AI glasses with SDK and web app support, the V207 SDK for upcoming Meta VR Glasses, and the launch of Horizon Create and Studio for prompt-driven game development.

## AI Models, APIs, and Development Tools

* **Muse Model Family Expansion:** Meta Superintelligence Labs released 10 models and products over the past few months, tailored for reasoning, media, and voice.
  * **Muse Spark 1.3:** Competes at the frontier with max reasoning capabilities, allowing developers to delegate toughest problems to teams of sub-agents. Consistently a top-two model on OpenCode Go, powering over 120 million sessions and 79 trillion tokens.
  * **Muse Spark on OpenRouter:** Reached over 2 trillion tokens per week within eight weeks of launch, with over 90% of tokens coming from AI-native companies and professional developers.
  * **Muse Image:** Launched in August for programmatic generation of production-grade images at scale.
  * **Muse Voice Transcribe:** Features state-of-the-art speech-to-text performance at launch, with text-to-speech and voice-to-voice capabilities planned.
* **Muse Code CLI Agent:** A terminal-installed coding agent powered by Muse Spark, featuring multi-agent parallel execution in isolated workspaces, structured planning for long-horizon work, and predictable flat-rate subscription pricing.
* **Open-Weight Form Factors:** Meta expanded developer access with two distinct open-weight models:
  * **Muse Glimmer:** A 30-billion dense model for always-on local agents that runs on a single GPU or Mac Mini, available under an Apache 2.0 license.
  * **Muse Spark 1.2:** Open weights will soon be released directly to the developer community.
* **Meta Model API General Availability:** Now generally available globally for enterprise-scale workloads, featuring standard production tiers with zero data training and a contributor tier offering frontier intelligence at up to 80% below standard rates. Also available via Oracle Cloud AI platform and in private preview with Google Cloud.
* **Meta Global AI Hackathon:** Kicks off virtually this October, backed by free API credits and a $1 million cash prize pool.

## Wearables and AI Glasses SDKs

* **AI Glasses Growth:** Usage of Meta AI glasses has tripled in the last year, with millions of users worldwide relying on context, voice UI, and agentic capabilities for "mental offload."
* **Device Access Toolkit Extensions:** Allows mobile apps to tap into AI glasses context (camera, microphone, sensors). New updates add advanced camera capture controls, motion and speech capabilities (using IMU data for gaze-aware experiences like bird identification), and voice invocation via the Meta AI wake word.
* **Web Apps Toolkit & Web MCP Support:** Enables web standards to build new experiences for Meta Ray-Ban displays, with web MCP support allowing agentic control of web apps through single-line-of-code voice commands.
* **Discovery Surfaces:** Two new surfaces allow users to discover developer apps: direct on-device discovery on Meta Ray-Ban Display, and a curated section in the Meta AI app.
* **New York Times Cooking Partnership:** Integrated their mobile app with AI glasses using the Device Access Toolkit and Neural Band gesture navigation to launch a hands-free cooking mode this fall.
* **Meta AI Connectors:** Developer preview launched for connecting services directly into Meta AI and Muse without users leaving the conversation.

## VR Glasses and Quest Ecosystem

* **Meta VR Glasses and SDK V207:** Meta VR Glasses ship in 2027, but SDK V207 is live immediately. The glasses are light (~100 grams), controller-free (using eye, hand, and voice tracking), and backward compatible with controllers.
* **Developer Readiness and Agentic Workflows:** Features full agentic workflows for VR across game engines, Android, and web tools (Meta XR Operator and Immersive Web Emulation Runtime), enabling tasks like frame rate optimization in 15 minutes.
* **Testing and Simulation Tools:** 
  * **XR Simulator:** Test full VR scenes on desktop with glasses inputs via webcam.
  * **Spatial Simulator:** Desktop emulator running real OS pieces for 2D Android apps with pin-mode checking.
  * **Field of View Emulator:** Preview Quest apps on VR glasses fields of view.
* **Store Performance and Benchmarks:** Store search rebuilt for intent, categories, and misspellings, increasing daily searches by 15%+ and user conversions by 20%+. Major updates launched for the Benchmarks tool, including peer sets.
* **Meta VR Start Developer Competition:** Second annual competition launched with an $1 million prize pool and an 8-week build window.

## Horizon Game Creation Engine

* **Horizon Create (Mobile):** A mobile app where users can play community games and build playable 2D/3D games using natural language prompts while on the go.
* **Horizon Studio (Web/Browser):** A browser-based one-stop-shop tool running with desktop-grade depth. Features visual editing, scene views, script parameters, and **Canvas Mode** (a structured map of game logic, enemies, and leveling that populates automatically). Also acts as a live ops partner post-publishing.
* **Feed Distribution:** Published games are instantly available on Horizon and surfaced directly in Facebook and Instagram feeds without app downloads or store page navigation.
* **Future Collaborative Vision:** Real-time, collaborative multi-creator development in a shared world supported by a swarm of AI agents is currently in closed Alpha and opening broadly in coming weeks.

## Predictions & Forward Calls

* **Meta VR Glasses release timeline:** Meta VR Glasses will ship in 2027. — Jamie Keane

## Notable Quotes

> "If we only think about AI in terms of efficiency, we miss the bigger opportunity: invention. Because AI doesn't just help you build faster, it allows developers to invent more, and people who never thought that they could build, now can."
> — **Vishal Shah**

> "When you give developers a level playing field, they pick Muse models for their hardest agentic work, and at a tier that lets them scale."
> — **Shashank Goyal**

> "We call it hands-free mode, but, really, it enables you to use your hands for everything other than scrolling a recipe. Your hands are wet or mid-chop, or in gloves or oven mitts. The best hands-free experience respects that you're focused on the task at hand."
> — **A.J. Chavar**

briefings.title: Patrick Collison on Claude Code at Stripe
briefings.tldr: About 36% of Stripe's pull requests now start as a prompt using Claude Code in isolated dev boxes, enabling massive productivity gains—such as one engineer merging 600 AI-written pull requests with only a single revert—while maintaining the company's five and a half nines of reliability.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
About 36% of Stripe's pull requests now start as a prompt using Claude Code in isolated dev boxes, enabling massive productivity gains—such as one engineer merging 600 AI-written pull requests with only a single revert—while maintaining the company's five and a half nines of reliability.

## Claude Code Adoption & Scale at Stripe
* **Core Metrics & Usage:** 
  * **36% of pull requests:** Now originate as a prompt executed by Claude Code running in isolated dev boxes.
  * **600 AI-written pull requests:** Completed by a single Stripe engineer in H1 with exactly one revert.
  * **Quality impact:** Quality per pull request has increased over the last 18 months, while total reliability remains steady at five and a half nines despite a slight rise in minor incidents.
* **Workflow & Orchestration:** 
  * **Pre-installed dev boxes:** Every dev box comes with Claude Code pre-installed as the default starting point for median engineering tasks.
  * **"Minions" orchestration:** Engineers use Slack or web interfaces to orchestrate VMs via prompts, spinning up fully new VMs to run tasks end-to-end through test suites.
  * **Plan Mode & Parallel Execution:** Engineers use advanced planning models to construct complex execution plans, then dispatch up to 10 parallel dev boxes to work simultaneously across multiple days.

## Product Development & Architectural Velocity
* **Stripe Projects Case Study:** 
  * **Scope & Timeline:** Built from first idea to public launch in 8 weeks by 2 to 3 engineers, integrating with roughly 50 different external services (such as PostHog and Vercel).
  * **Productivity multiplier:** Estimated by engineers to be at least a 6x speedup compared to pre-AI methods (which would have required a larger team and six months).
* **Codebase as a Prompt:** 
  * **Architectural improvements:** Stripe is undertaking more projects to improve architecture and codebases, operating under the philosophy that "every code base is now the prompt for another code base."
  * **Idea translation:** The friction of unfinished projects ("graveyard of projects") has largely disappeared; shower thoughts now translate into actual existence at a much higher rate, raising the returns on curiosity.

## Infrastructure Guardrails & Security
* **Deterministic Guarantees:** 
  * **Hard barriers over subjectivity:** Reliability is maintained by relying on invariants and hard infrastructural barriers rather than probabilistic or discretionary checks.
  * **Data tagging legacy:** Investments started in 2017 in semantically aware data tagging, granular permissioning, and prompt injection protection have accidentally positioned Stripe exceptionally well for agentic development.
* **Defense Advantage:** Patrick Collison predicts that in equilibrium over the next couple of years, AI will become substantially "defense adventaging" as automated observability, instrumentation, and harnesses catch issues early.

## Startup Ecosystem & Economic Data
* **Surging Firm Creation:** 
  * **2x new businesses:** The number of new businesses launching on Stripe per unit time is up by roughly a factor of two—representing the largest relative acceleration in Stripe's 15-year history.
  * **Startup share:** Approximately a quarter of all Delaware corporations are incorporated with Stripe.
  * **Global reach & outcomes:** The surge is broad-based across most countries, with average revenue per new business increasing, and significant jumps in businesses reaching $100k or $1M revenue thresholds.
* **Micro-Data vs. Macro-Data:** Micro-data refutes concerns of a centralized economy, showing more new firm creation, higher success rates, and improved growth rates.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Patrick Collison:** AI will on net make Stripe quite a bit more reliable over the next year or two through new observability, instrumentation, and automated scrutiny.
* **Patrick Collison:** In equilibrium in a couple of years, AI will be substantially "defense adventaging."
* **Patrick Collison:** Most transactions will be between agents within three years.

## Notable Quotes
> "The number of new businesses launching on Stripe per unit time is up by roughly a factor of two."
> — Patrick Collison

> "Every code base is now the prompt for another code base."
> — Patrick Collison (referencing a Stripe friend)

briefings.title: Peter Thiel: The AI Crisis, Europe’s Decline & the Battle for America
briefings.channel: MDMEETS - Essential Talks with Mathias Döpfner
briefings.tldr: Peter Thiel argues that artificial intelligence has broken decades of technological stagnation, but warns that the West—especially Europe—is falling severely behind China and the US, while societal polarization and broken intergenerational compacts threaten democratic stability.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Peter Thiel argues that artificial intelligence has broken decades of technological stagnation, but warns that the West—especially Europe—is falling severely behind China and the US, while societal polarization and broken intergenerational compacts threaten democratic stability.

## AI Progress & Global Competition
- **Stagnation Broken by AI:** Thiel notes that his 20-year-old stagnation thesis (slow progress in atoms since the 1970s) has been proven true in retrospect, but AI now has the potential to reaccelerate growth.
- **The China Factor:** China acts as a fast follower in AI, and Thiel warns that Western anti-AI sentiment and precautionary regulations (such as papal encyclicals) effectively act as "useful idiot" support for the Chinese Communist Party.
- **Palantir Corporate Urgency:** Sales of Palantir to US corporations have accelerated tremendously due to a corporate urgency to master AI transformation, a sense of urgency notably absent in Europe.
- **Moralizing Technology:** Thiel criticizes the tendency to moralize technology rather than viewing it functionally, arguing that tools are neutral and that societies focus too much on good-versus-evil debates while tolerating 99% incompetence.

## Politics, Democracy & Polarization
- **The Growth Deficit:** Western democracies are in trouble primarily because they lack a broad growth story of the future, leading to zero-sum politics that empower extreme right and left parties.
- **The 2009 Essay Controversy:** Revisiting his controversial 2009 statement questioning the compatibility of freedom and democracy, Thiel clarifies that he was advocating for a depoliticization and de-intensification of politics among libertarians, not the removal of voters.
- **Rise of the Democratic Socialists:** Thiel highlights the explosive growth of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA)—growing from 5,000 to 50,000 members with median age shifting from 66 to 33 post-2016—calling the far-left takeover of the Democratic party a catastrophic risk.
- **Gerontocracy & The Linka:** In Germany and Europe, parties like *Die Linke* gain traction among young voters (47% of 16-24 year olds in Berlin) by tapping into real economic frustrations like skyrocketing rents, exposing how societies are run for older generations.
- **Trump and Establishment Failure:** Trump's rise reflected a systemic failure of the establishment to address long-term growth, globalization, and endless Middle Eastern entanglements, though Thiel critiques the first administration's infighting and the second administration's overcorrected loyalty tests.
- **Macroeconomic Brinkmanship:** Thiel warns that post-2008 reliance on runaway deficits with non-zero interest rates is reaching a breaking point, forcing a choice between socialist taxation, severe austerity, or a systemic financial wall.

## Europe's Decline & The Entrepreneurial Drought
- **Concorde vs. Minitel:** Comparing Europe's AI prospects to historical industrial efforts, Thiel assesses that Europe is currently further behind in AI than France's failed Minitel program.
- **Fear of Success:** Beyond a fear of failure, Thiel argues Germany suffers from a "fear of success"—a reluctance to scale companies aggressively like Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.
- **Inherited Wealth Statistics:** Citing demographic wealth data, Thiel points out that while the top 50 German wealthiest individuals include 20 Gen X or younger members, *all 20* inherited their fortunes, whereas in the US, 9 out of 12 Gen X/younger top wealth holders made their own money.
- **Geopolitical Alignment:** Thiel asserts it is in Europe's best interest to be a reliable ally to the US rather than equating the US and China morally.

## Health Longevity & Transhumanism
- **Abandonment of the Curing of Death:** Thiel laments the social decline that caused modern society to give up on early Enlightenment goals (Francis Bacon, Benjamin Franklin) of curing aging and death.
- **Biological Information Science:** Framing biological processes as potentially reversible if understood as computational information science, Thiel views physical aging and mortality as problems to be actively solved.
- **Concrete Focus on Dementia:** Among longevity and biotech investments, Thiel prioritizes finding a way to slow or reverse brain decline and dementia in the years ahead.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- *No genuine forward-looking claims with specific concrete timeframes, timelines, or numerical targets were made in the transcript.*

## Notable Quotes
> "If you're evil, you're at least competent... and if you're evil, you're not bad and therefore you're actually maybe you're actually kind of kind of good because you're at least getting something done."
> — Peter Thiel

> "The Pope's encyclical was working for the Communist Party. I'm not saying he was an agent of the Communists, but he was at least acting as a useful idiot for the CCP."
> — Peter Thiel

> "In the US, nine out of 12 of those people [Gen X or younger among the wealthiest] made their own money. In Germany, all 20 of those 20 inherited it. Not a single person did something new, made some new money, built a large new scalable company."
> — Peter Thiel

briefings.title: Re-Founding Incumbents for the AI Era with Sequence Holdings Co-Founder and CEO Michael Lee
briefings.channel: No Priors: AI, Machine Learning, Tech, & Startups
briefings.tldr: Sequence Holdings Co-Founder and CEO Michael Lee joins Sarah Guo to discuss Sequence's $7.7 billion take-private transaction of Baldwin with the Dell Family Office, and explains why permanent holding company structures and frontier engineering can transform market incumbents from the inside out.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Sequence Holdings Co-Founder and CEO Michael Lee joins Sarah Guo to discuss Sequence's $7.7 billion take-private transaction of Baldwin with the Dell Family Office, and explains why permanent holding company structures and frontier engineering can transform market incumbents from the inside out.

## Company Overview & Structure
- **Sequence Holdings:** Founded 20 months ago by Michael Lee and co-founder Alex, operating as a permanent holding company partnering with management teams to buy and refound businesses into market leaders using AI.
- **The Permanent Holding Company Model:** 
  - Aligns the duration of capital with sustained operational commitments and end-to-end transformation.
  - Culturally oriented around forging market leaders rather than deploying capital on short fund timelines.
  - Leverages retained earnings to support existing portfolio companies and net-new investments.
- **Why Ownership Beats Services and Software:**
  - **In-house hiring limit:** Traditional Fortune 500 companies cannot easily recruit and retain top-tier engineering talent because their celebrated persona is typically the investor, not the engineer.
  - **Services misalignment:** Consulting and service providers (e.g., Accenture, McKinsey) optimize for getting into and growing a client's wallet, leading to incrementalism rather than structural change.
  - **Software limitations:** Enterprise software is built on historical homogeneous workflows designed around existing human assembly lines, missing new paradigms.
- **Scarcity & Focus:** Sequence aims to do only **one deal per year**, avoiding traditional fund deployment pressures and focusing intensely on business quality and team.

## Baldwin Transaction ($7.7B Take-Private)
- **The Deal:** Announced the largest AI take-private transaction to date: Baldwin for **$7.7 billion**, executed in partnership with the Dell Family Office (DFO).
- **Partnership & Control:** Sequence and DFO are co-controlling Baldwin together, with DFO providing the crucial certainty of capital required for the multi-billion-dollar commitment letter.
- **Why Baldwin (Insurance Brokerage):**
  - Represents a **$2 trillion+** annual gross written premium market with extreme defensiveness and 90% gross retention rates.
  - Features carriers that generate most of their profit from investing rather than underwriting, heavily incentivizing asset gathering and broker distribution.
  - Characterized by centralized operations and a management team (led by CEO Trevor Baldwin) that was already early in adopting technologies like Anthropic end-to-end and running on a single instance of Applied Epic (core AMS).

## BankSouth Pilot & Real-World Results
- **The Genesis:** Started as a customer engagement in August 2024 through Jamie Reynolds (co-founder of Aanir) whose family owns BankSouth in Georgia. Sequence operated in a services motion from August to November before investing for a minority stake, closing the investment in March after Fed and OCC approval.
- **Regulated Banking as a Feature:** Regulatory oversight provided well-defined operations, excellent data hygiene, and centralized underwriting physics that scale easily across branches.
- **Concrete Results (Post-March Investment):**
  - **Consumer Underwriting Speed:** Average consumer loan underwriting time decreased by **94%** since March.
  - **Commercial Underwriting Speed:** Average commercial loan lifecycle dropped from **30 days to 11 days**.
  - **Volume Capacity:** In Q2 relative to Q1, loan volumes **doubled** at the bank, handled with a significantly smaller underwriting team while maintaining exact underwriting standards (headcount shifted to higher-value roles: one retirement, one moved to front office).

## Platform Technology & Engineering Playbook
- **Atlas Platform:** Sequence's shared platform built at BankSouth and designed to generalize across industries, consisting of four layers:
  - **Data Ontology:** Defines the business and its motion in code to make data legible to models.
  - **Agent Builder:** Builds high-performance agents grounded in ground truth.
  - **Lattice:** The orchestration engine that instruments workflows using built agents.
  - **Artifacts:** The application builder sitting on top of the stack.
- **Engineering Philosophy:** About 80% of a business's atomic units are homogeneous and 20% vertically specific. Unlike application software, Sequence celebrates model performance improvements as an expansion of their toolkit.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
*(Note: No explicit timelines, numerical future targets, or conditional predictions with exact timeframes were stated as forward bets in the transcript; historical metrics and past results are detailed in the body sections above.)*

## Notable Quotes
> "In a world where you believe that alpha comes from engineering and AI, you need to create a culture whereby the celebrated persona is the engineer."
> — Michael Lee

> "We're one of the few business models in the world that's completely immune to what the model's going to do. As the model performances improve, we celebrate here at sequence..."
> — Michael Lee

> "Ideas are cheap and execution is really hard and like truly exceptional people will always figure out how to make something work."
> — Michael Lee

briefings.title: Up Next: A Conversation With Palmer Luckey

people.name: Jessica Peterson
people.role: Instructor Flight Test Engineer, U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School
people.organization: U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School

organizations: U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School
briefings.tldr: Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril Industries, discusses his vision for defense technology, moving away from cost-plus contracting toward high-speed product manufacturing modeled after the automotive industry, and highlights future battle spaces including subterranean operations and autonomous air systems.
briefings.summary_markdown:
- **TL;DR:** Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril Industries, discusses his vision for defense technology, moving away from cost-plus contracting toward high-speed product manufacturing modeled after the automotive industry, and highlights future battle spaces including subterranean operations and autonomous air systems.

## Speaker Roster & Event Context
- **Clay Mowry:** CEO of AIAA and host of *Up Next*
- **Jessica “STING” Peterson:** Instructor Flight Test Engineer at the U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School, serving as co-host ("wingman")
- **Palmer Luckey:** Founder of Anduril Industries (and former founder of Oculus VR), guest on the program
- **Setting:** Recorded on location at Anduril headquarters in Costa Mesa, California.

## Journey from Consumer Tech to Defense
- **Founding Oculus:** **Consumer Virtual Reality:** Started working on VR as a gamer and hobbyist to push past the limits of multi-monitor setups, ultimately selling Oculus to Facebook for $2.3 billion before turning 21.
- **Pivoting to National Security:** **Impact Over Fun:** After being fired from Facebook 3 years post-acquisition, evaluated solving obesity via zero-calorie foods and prison reform before choosing national security because the US tech community was reluctant to work with the defense apparatus.
- **Early Defense Exposure:** **Bravemind Program:** Worked for a few months before Oculus at the ICT Mixed Reality Lab on virtual reality exposure therapy (Bravemind) to treat veterans with PTSD.

## Manufacturing Strategy & Arsenal 1
- **Product Company vs. Contractor:** **Speculative Development:** Anduril operates as a product company using its own capital to build and test systems rather than relying on time-and-materials cost-plus contracts.
- **Automotive Model for Aerospace:** **Car Factory Manufacturing:** Luckey asserts that the US must design weapons (like missiles and aircraft) that can be built in existing car and tractor factories, emulating World War II manufacturing scaling.
- **Arsenal 1 Facility:** **5 Million Square Feet:** Anduril's massive new Ohio facility utilizes automotive-style tools and processes rather than bespoke aerospace manufacturing.
- **Intellectual Property & Patents:** **Trade Secrets Over Patents:** Luckey avoids patents, calling them "Chinese instruction manuals" that block Western allies while adversaries freely copy them, preferring trade secrets and government-owned interoperability standards.

## Unmanned Platforms & Autonomy
- **Fury and Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA):** **FQ44 Designation:** The prototype YFQ-44A has moved to serial production as the FQ44, fulfilling Luckey's goal of securing an official unmanned fighter ("Q") designation.
- **Thunder Hybrid-Electric VTOL:** **Jet Fuel Reliance:** Thunder is a high-speed, long-range tilt-rotor aircraft powered primarily by jet fuel (partnering with Archer for composite structures and drivetrains) serving as a "loyal wingman" for attack helicopters.
- **Autonomous Deterrence:** **Human Safety in Conflict:** Luckey argues that adversaries only believe the US will deploy systems that do not put human lives at risk, giving autonomous systems a massive deterrence advantage.
- **Counter-UAS & Micro-Defense:** **Helicopter Protection:** Suggests that adapting technologies like the Trophy active protection system to aircraft will enable helicopters to easily shoot down incoming drones using small-caliber guns.

## Interoperability, AI, & Testing
- **Lattis Ecosystem:** **Open Integration:** Lattis integrates with over 100 existing DoD platforms and has approximately 700 companies in its partner program.
- **Enforcing Standards:** **Testing Interoperability:** Luckey stresses that the government must actively test and enforce interoperability standards rather than accepting contractors' claims at face value.
- **Rigorous Edge-Case Testing:** **Worst-Case Scenarios:** Testing must simulate high-workload, degraded conditions (such as hydraulics-out or GPS jamming) during early design phases.
- **The "Steve Jobs" Critique:** **High Skill Ceilings:** Luckey laments the "iPhone-ization" of technology, arguing that touch screens and simplified UIs sacrifice long-term efficiency and skill ceilings for ease of first-minute use.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Subterranean Warfare:** Palmer Luckey predicts that the subterranean domain will become a major new warfare domain, with autonomous vehicles utilizing the Earth's crust as a 3D maneuver and battle space.
- **Government Nationalization of Designs:** Palmer Luckey anticipates that in a major shooting war, the US government will nationalize Anduril's designs and farm them out to mass-production partners because Arsenal 1 alone will be insufficient.
- **Bullet-on-Bullet Aerial Defense:** Palmer Luckey predicts that on a not-too-distant timeframe, radar will enable aircraft to track bullets and shoot incoming projectiles and quadcopters out of the air using other projectiles.

## Notable Quotes
> "We need to design missiles that can be made in car factories. We need to design aircraft that can be made in tractor factories. They're not waiting to be invented. They're waiting to be implemented."
> — Palmer Luckey

> "I often call patents Chinese instruction manuals. You're just putting everything out there for an adversary to rip off."
> — Palmer Luckey

> "I think that we're going to see the subterranean domain... the real deal no subt fight where you are using the crust of the earth as a three-dimensional maneuver and battle space."
> — Palmer Luckey
